citation: Burbulla LF et al. Mitochondrial proteolytic stress induced by loss of mortalin function is rescued by Parkin and PINK1. Cell Death Dis. 2014. doi:10.1038/cddis.2014.103. PMID:24743735.
description: This paper showed that reduced mortalin/HSPA9 function activates mitochondrial unfolded-protein stress, increases mitochondrial fragmentation and mitophagy, and sensitizes cells to apoptosis. It is direct target-specific support that HSPA9 loss produces mitochondrial proteostatic stress.

citation: Zhu JY et al. Knockdown of Hsc70-5/mortalin induces loss of synaptic mitochondria in a Drosophila Parkinson's disease model. PLoS One. 2013. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0083714. PMID:24386261.
description: Drosophila mortalin knockdown reduced ATP, fragmented mitochondria, caused early loss of synaptic mitochondria, and preferentially affected dopaminergic neurons. It supports transfer of HSPA9/mortalin mitochondrial stress biology into neurons while leaving species and developmental differences.

citation: Zhou Z, Fan Y, Zong R, Tan K. The mitochondrial unfolded protein response: A multitasking giant in the fight against human diseases. Ageing Res Rev. 2022. doi:10.1016/j.arr.2022.101702. PMID:35908669.
description: This review summarizes the mammalian UPRmt and describes eIF2alpha phosphorylation with CHOP, ATF4, and ATF5 as core transcriptional mediators. It supplies the stress-transcription link used to interpret Chac1, Ddit3, Lonp1, amino-acid transporter, and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase induction after Hspa9 perturbation.

citation: Hamazaki J, Murata S. ER-Resident Transcription Factor Nrf1 Regulates Proteasome Expression and Beyond. Int J Mol Sci. 2020. doi:10.3390/ijms21103683. PMID:32456207.
description: This review states that the 26S proteasome recognizes ubiquitinated proteins in an ATP-dependent manner and that Nrf1/NFE2L1 coordinates expression of proteasome subunit genes after proteasome impairment. It predicts proteasome-subunit bounce-back after loss of an ATPase regulatory-particle subunit.

citation: Chandran A, Oliver HJ, Rochet JC. Role of NFE2L1 in the Regulation of Proteostasis: Implications for Aging and Neurodegenerative Diseases. Biology. 2023. doi:10.3390/biology12091169. PMID:37759569.
description: This review describes NFE2L1 as the transcription factor primarily responsible for proteasome-inhibitor bounce-back, binding antioxidant-response elements in proteasome-subunit promoters under proteasome impairment. It supports the expectation that UPS compromise increases PSM genes.

citation: Aharoni S et al. PSMC1 variant causes a novel neurological syndrome. Clin Genet. 2022. doi:10.1111/cge.14195. PMID:35861243.
description: This report identifies PSMC1 as a 19S regulatory-particle ATPase whose ATP-binding-domain mutation causes a severe neurological syndrome and only partially rescues Drosophila Rpt2 silencing. It anchors PSMC1 to 19S proteasome ATPase function in nervous-system phenotypes.

citation: Yu ZQ et al. PSMC5 insufficiency and P320R mutation impair proteasome function. Hum Mol Genet. 2024. doi:10.1093/hmg/ddae085. PMID:38776958.
description: This paper shows that PSMC5 is an AAA ATPase subunit of the 19S regulatory particle and that PSMC5 insufficiency impairs proteasome function and activates apoptosis. It provides direct target support for interpreting Psmc5 perturbation as proteasome impairment.

citation: Markmiller S et al. Minor class splicing shapes the zebrafish transcriptome during development. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA. 2014. doi:10.1073/pnas.1305536111. PMID:24516132.
description: The zebrafish caliban model carries an rnpc3 mutation that impairs U12-type splicing and disrupts genes involved in mRNA processing through intron retention or altered gene expression. It supports a specific RNPC3-to-minor-spliceosome bridge, but not exact gene-level directions in this screen.

citation: Doggett K et al. Early developmental arrest and impaired gastrointestinal homeostasis in U12-dependent splicing-defective Rnpc3-deficient mice. RNA. 2018. doi:10.1261/rna.068221.118. PMID:30254136.
description: Conditional Rnpc3 loss in adult mice caused tissue degeneration and increased U12-type intron retention in tested transcripts. It confirms that RNPC3 is required for U12-dependent splicing in adult mammalian tissue, while the assayed tissue and intron-level readout differ from the Perturb-seq screen.

citation: Wu W, Ahmad K, Henikoff S. Chromatin-bound U2AF2 splicing factor ensures exon inclusion. Mol Cell. 2025. doi:10.1016/j.molcel.2025.04.013. PMID:40315850.
description: CUT&RUN and knockdown data show that U2AF2 binds chromatin over intron-containing genes and improves exon selection, including within genes encoding splicing factors. It supports a mechanistic U2AF2-to-splicing-factor bridge, not a direct prediction for total Rsrp1 or Mfsd2b abundance.

citation: Hu D et al. CDC40 suppression induces CDCA5 splicing defects and anti-proliferative effects in lung cancer cells. Sci Rep. 2025. doi:10.1038/s41598-024-83337-z. PMID:39747150.
description: CDC40 knockdown in lung cancer cells caused global transcriptional and splicing changes, enriched intron retention, and perturbation of splicing- and translation-related genes. It supports a CDC40-to-splicing-defect bridge but was not in neurons and did not validate the exact Pde4a/Rsrp1 module measured here.

citation: Clifton NE et al. Setd1a Loss-of-function Disrupts Epigenetic Regulation of Ribosomal Genes via Altered DNA Methylation. Schizophr Bull. 2026. doi:10.1093/schbul/sbaf091. PMID:40500874.
description: Developmental profiling of Setd1a+/- mouse frontal cortex reported downregulated mitochondrial gene expression while testing complex I activity. The result directionally supports a decrease in nuclear mitochondrial/OXPHOS transcripts after Setd1a loss.

citation: Mukai J et al. Recapitulation and Reversal of Schizophrenia-Related Phenotypes in Setd1a-Deficient Mice. Neuron. 2019. doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2019.09.014. PMID:31606247.
description: Setd1a-deficient mice showed cortical transcriptional changes in Setd1a-bound targets that are highly expressed in pyramidal neurons and had reversible adult phenotypes. It supports transport of Setd1a chromatin regulation into mouse neurons, although the perturbation was germline heterozygosity rather than acute CRISPR.
